label: No Ohio Marriage Amendment Vote
detail: Ohio voters do not face a state constitutional amendment on same-sex marriage when they vote for president.
assumption: Without the ballot measure, turnout among socially conservative Ohio voters is slightly lower and marriage is a less salient issue in Ohio, with other voters otherwise behaving as observed.
facts_text: Ohio's ballot on 2 November carries no state constitutional amendment on same-sex marriage, because the petition drive to place one there did not qualify.
Ohioans will vote on the presidential race and other offices without a state marriage question before them.
research_questions: How much did state same-sex marriage amendments on the ballot raise turnout among conservative or evangelical voters in 2004?
Did Ohio voters who supported the marriage amendment vote differently for president than similar voters in states without one?
How salient was same-sex marriage compared with the economy and Iraq for Ohio swing voters in 2004?
source_text: Ohio has no same-sex marriage amendment on its 2004 ballot.
